The suspect was charged with resisting an officer without violence.
The suspect was issued a $500 bond, which she later posted.
She attended court without a lawyer, waived her right to counsel, and pleaded no contest.
The judge withheld adjudication and placed her on probation for four months,
ordering her to complete an anger management course within three months,
along with 25 hours of community service.
A month later, she wrote a letter to the judge to appeal her no contest plea and request a public defender.
The court granted the motion to withdraw the plea in sentence and appointed her a public defender.
In court, the defense filed a plea of not guilty and requested a jury trial.
Before any trial happened, she pleaded no contest again and was ordered to pay all fines and court costs.
She later failed to pay her court ordered costs and fees on time.

legal.disposition: Initial plea of no contest, later withdrawn, then no contest again; fines and court costs ordered; later failed to pay.
